sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Sleep** is a status effect in *Elden Ring*, incapacitating most lesser enemies for an extended period of time or inflicting heavy stagger towards stronger enemies and players alike as well as draining a chunk of the player's FP, making it into a slightly less dangerous version of Madness. The player's resistance to this status ailment is determined by their Focus stat, which is increased by the Mind stat.

sections.heading: Mechanics
sections.markdown:
Inflicting Sleep on a player will briefly stagger them, even through a roll, and drains FP equal to 30 + 10% of max FP.
Inflicting on most generic enemies will briefly stagger them.

Sleep has special interactions with certain enemies: some, like the Godskin Apostle and Godskin Noble, Vulgar Militia, and Mad Pumpkin Heads, will fall into a heavier sleep, making them vulnerable to a Critical Attack and potentially sleeping for up to a minute if not damaged. Others, enemies that ride other entities, will get knocked off their mount. This includes almost all enemies on horseback (such as Godrick Knights, Cuckoo Knights, Leyndell Knights, and Kaiden Sellswords) but also the Giant Ant-riding Nox Swordstresses but doesn't include Night's Cavalry (since they are immune to Sleep) or Tree Sentinels (since them and their horse are effectively one entity).

sections.heading: Eternal Sleep
sections.markdown: A special variant of Sleep introduced with Shadow of the Erdtree, Eternal Sleep has slightly different effects from regular Sleep. The FP drain to players is increased to 50 + 15% of max FP, weaker enemies such as Godrick Soldiers can potentially be slept permanently and never wake up, and bosses vulnerable to Sleep won't wake up the until 5 seconds after they were first attacked and aren't susceptible to Critical Attacks.

sections.heading: Spells
sections.markdown: There are no spells that inflict sleep in the game currently.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Skeletons** are Enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Skeletons are found all throughout the Lands Between and come in several different variants employing a myriad of different weapons.

They are vulnerable to Strike damage and most often vulnerable Holy damage. As they are part of Those Who Live in Death they are also very weak to certain holy based attacks such as the Golden Epitaph, Skill: Shared Order, and Holy Water Pot.

All skeletons also carry a trait unique to this enemy type where they do not die immediately upon having their health reduced to zero. Instead, after a few seconds, their remains begin to glow white and they can be finished off with any damage, or else they resurrect after another few seconds, now with full health.

This resurrection mechanics can be skipped by killing them with certain weapons more effective against Those Who Live in Death.

There is also a version of the regular Skeleton variant, found only in Black Knife Catacombs, who cannot be finished off when defeated. Instead, they can only be dealt with permanently by killing one of the nearby Necromancer variant Commoners that otherwise keep them "alive".

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.markdown: Skeleton warriors found only on the surface (and within Sage's Cave) they carry a wide variety of weapons and clothes that help distinguish them from each other. They can be found in graveyards all across the Lands Between and many of them are linked to local Tibia Mariners, meaning should certain local Mariner's be felled, then the presence of these skeletons may fade from several nearby graveyards as a result.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown: These enemies are often encountered in groups, with Grave Wardens and Crossbow Militiamen providing range support while Knights close in from the front while blocking attacks and Bandits use their jump attacks.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.markdown: Heavily built skeletons wielding greataxes and halberds, they have much greater poise than normal skeletons and will attack sequentially as long a Tarnished remains near.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.markdown: Skeletons with golden bones, they share most of their moveset with the normal counterparts however with the addition of an attack that involves them gliding around the air like a kite while spewing magic gas beneath them. They've also shed most of their frailty against holy damage.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown: As these are so similar to the base variant of the skeleton, their sudden flight is likely to prove quite a scare when first encountered. Additionally, their existence is largely limited to one graveyard in Altus Plateau that is just east of Hermit Merchant (Capital Outskirts).

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.markdown: Same as the normal Skeleton variant, except only encountered in Crumbling Farum Azula.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.markdown: These skeleton boasts most of the same moveset as their humanoid counterpart, however they have additional fire breath attacks, slightly more resilience to Holy Damage but less resilience to Fire Damage.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.markdown: These skeletons are found exclusively in Catacombs and Hero's Graves. They carry no vestigial remains of clothes or armor of any kind and are generally distinguished from each other purely depending on the weapons they carry.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown: - The catacomb variant greatly resembles the skeletons found in FromSoftwares earlier Dark Souls series.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Scarabs**, also known as **Teardrop Scarabs**, are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Scarabs are beetles found throughout the Lands Between, typically rolling balls of various colors, which indicate the type of item they drop when killed. Scarabs are sources of valuable resources such as spells, ashes of war, smithing stones, and replenishments for the Sacred Flasks. They come in various colors and sizes, each bearing an eye on their thorax.

Scarabs are non-hostile wildlife that flee when approached. They roll their precious dung away from perceived threats before vanishing. Some scarabs are nearly invisible, leaving only tracks on the ground that follow a set pattern, making them predictable to hit. Certain scarabs can also fly, hovering in place until attacked. In rare cases, scarabs will explode when attacked, killing themselves and damaging nearby foes.

The laborious beetles abandoned their treasured balls and returned home when it was time for them to die.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.markdown: Red Crimson Teardrop Scarabs that roll balls of golden twigs filled with crimson tears.

sections.heading: Drops
sections.markdown: When killed, they will restore charges to the Flask of Crimson Tears.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.markdown: Blue Cerulean Teardrop Scarabs that roll balls of golden twigs filled with cerulean tears.

sections.heading: Drops
sections.markdown: When killed, they will restore charges to the Flask of Cerulean Tears.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.markdown: Grey scarabs that roll clumps of ash. When killed, they drop Ashes of War which can be added to weapons to apply affinities and skills.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.markdown: Blue-green scarabs that roll clumps of glintstone. When killed, they drop sorceries.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.markdown: Golden scarabs that roll clumps of stone containing incantations, which they drop when killed.

sections.heading: Variant Description
sections.markdown: Grey scarabs that roll clumps of stone. They drop smithing stones when killed.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.markdown: Scarabs are found throughout the Lands Between and the Realm of Shadow.

sections.heading: Moveset
sections.markdown: Scarabs typically have no attacks and will flee. Some scarabs may detonate themselves, dealing area-of-effect damage. Other scarabs teleport instantaneously when attacked. These scarabs have simply moved to a predetermined location nearby.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- There are six different colors for scarabs.
- Nearby scarabs play a sound cue.
- Scarabs disappear after fleeing from the player. This is forewarned by a series of sound and visual cues and is interrupted when the scarab takes damage.
- Scarabs that have disappeared can be reencountered after resting at a Site of Grace.
- Those that drop unique loot, such as Ashes of War, will no longer respawn once defeated.
- Scarabs that refill the Flask of Crimson Tears and Flask of Cerulean Tears will respawn.
- The Gold Scarab and Silver Scarab talismans provide bonuses to Runes earned and Item Discovery respectively.
- There are five headgear items based on scarabs: the Ash-of-War Scarab, Cerulean Tear Scarab, Crimson Tear Scarab, Glintstone Scarab, and Incantation Scarab.
- Scarabs drop Talismans in Elden Ring Nightreign. They respawn after disappearing.
- The scarab is the seal of the Everdark Sovereigns and appears on the Collector Signboard in *Nightreign*.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:

- The symbol displayed on the Gold and Silver Scarab talismans also appears on the Crimson Teardrop Scarab depicted in the icon for About Teardrop Scarabs. A different icon appears on the bodies of Teardrop Scarabs in-game.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Shabriri** is an NPC in Elden Ring. He is a spirit that possesses the body of Bloody Finger Hunter Yura, appearing after the player ascends the Grand Lift of Rold. Note that once Shabriri appears, Yura's questline will end regardless of how much progress has been made in it. It is not necessary to have started or completed Yura's questline for Shabriri to appear. If player visits the Three Fingers before reaching Shabriri, he will not appear. The Ronin's Set can be found on the ground where he would otherwise stand.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown: The most reviled man in all history, Shabriri was found guilty of slander long ago and sentenced to blindness. With his eyeballs completely gouged out, it is said that, in time, the Frenzied Flame came to dwell within his empty sockets. He believed that chaos should take the world and was regarded to be the origin of the sickness of Frenzied Flame. Following his death, Shabriri endured as a spirit capable of inhabiting the bodies of others.

sections.heading: Game Events
sections.markdown: The Tarnished encounters Shabriri in the Mountaintops of the Giants, where he is inhabiting the body of Bloody Finger Hunter Yura. The Tarnished, at the behest of Melina, is bound for the Forge of the Giants so she may set the Erdtree aflame. However, Shabriri advises the Tarnished to seek out the Three Fingers in the depths below Leyndell, revealing that their ascendency to the throne of Elden Lord would otherwise require Melina's sacrifice. He proposes an alternative path: the Tarnished may spare the life of Melina by inheriting the flame of frenzy and using their own body as kindling. Shabriri bids the Tarnished become the Lord of Chaos, burning the Erdtree to the ground and incinerating all that divides and distinguishes.

sections.heading: Location
sections.markdown: Shabriri is found near the Zamor Ruins Site of Grace on the Mountaintops of the Giants.

sections.heading: Summon Sign
sections.markdown: Shabriri is a summonable cooperator for the Godfrey, First Elden Lord / Hoarah Loux, Warrior boss fight if the player has visited the Three Fingers and has not used Miquella's Needle.

sections.heading: Character Information
sections.markdown:
- Shabriri can be attacked and killed at the Mountaintops of the Giants ( 3,107 HP).
- Drops: 1,000, Iron Kasa, Ronin's Armor, Ronin's Gauntlets, and Ronin's Greaves.
- The version of Shabriri at the Mountaintops of the Giants can cast one extra spell: Inescapable Frenzy.

sections.heading: Shabriri's Quest
sections.markdown: - Shabriri's questline intersects with the following NPCs: Bloody Finger Hunter Yura, Melina

sections.heading: Questline Steps
sections.markdown:
1. Mountaintops of the Giants
 - Shabriri can be found by the Zamor Ruins Site of Grace near the beginning of the Mountaintops of the Giants area. Exhaust his dialogue to unlock new dialogue from Melina when resting at a Site of Grace.
1. Frenzied Flame Proscription
 - Travel to the Frenzied Flame Proscription through the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds and Cathedral of the Forsaken. Remove all of your armor and interact with the door on the lowest floor for a cutscene in which the Three Fingers embrace you. This can be done regardless of whether you have met Shabriri already. Doing so will cause Shabriri to disappear from his previous location.
 - This will unlock the Lord of Frenzied Flame Ending. This will lock you out of achieving any of the other endings unless you obtain Miquella's Needle by completing Millicent's quest and defeating Malenia, Blade of Miquella, and using it in Dragonlord Placidusax's boss room.
1. *(Optional)* Leyndell, Ashen Capital
 - Shabriri will be available as a cooperator to assist with the fight against Godfrey, First Elden Lord at the Elden Throne if the player has not used Miquella's Needle.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Shabriri and Bloody Finger Hunter Yura wear the same armor set and have the same face data and voice actor; however, Shabriri does not use Yura's Nagakiba or battle art, instead wielding an Uchigatana with Impaling Thrust.
- Shabriri performs a unique gesture: he covers his eyes with both hands.
- Shabriri was said to have gained the Flame of Frenzy from reading the message imprinted on the tomb of an ancient god by the Readerless Fingers.
- The eyeballs of those afflicted with madness were called Shabriri Grapes. Lightseeker Hyetta, a blind maiden, is guided to the Three Fingers after consuming enough of them.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Skill: Spinning Slash** is a Skill in Elden Ring. It comes in two different variants carrying the same name, one is generic, is available as an Ash of War and is native to many different weapons (particularly among Curved Swords, Curved Greatswords, Twinblades, Halberds and Reapers). While the other variant, despite sharing the exact same name, has unique, additional Ice Lightning properties and only exists on one weapon, the Dragon Halberd.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
- Can be granted to infusable swords, axes, and halberds (except for Colossal Swords) with the Ash of War: Spinning Slash.
- Innate skill of many Straight Swords, Curved Swords, Curved Greatswords, Twinblades, Halberds, and Reapers.
 - Straight Swords: Crystal Sword, Rotten Crystal Sword, and Warhawk's Talon.
 - Curved Swords: Bandit's Curved Sword, Beastman's Curved Sword, Falchion, Flowing Curved Sword, Grossmesser, Mantis Blade, Scavenger's Curved Sword, Scimitar, Shamshir, and Shotel.
 - Curved Greatswords: Beastman's Cleaver, Dismounter, Freyja's Greatsword Shadow of the Erdtree, Omen Cleaver, and Monk's Flameblade.
 - Twinblades: Black Steel Twinblade Shadow of the Erdtree, Gargoyle's Twinblade, Gargoyle's Black Blades, Twinblade, and Twinned Knight Swords.
 - Halberds: Gargoyle's Black Halberd, Gargoyle's Halberd, Glaive, Guardian's Swordspear, Nightrider Glaive, Pest's Glaive, Ripple Crescent Halberd, Vulgar Militia Saw, and Vulgar Militia Shotel.
 - Reapers: Grave Scythe and Scythe.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown:
Spin once, hitting for 110% (105% with larger weapons and Twinblades) of Attack Power.

Using the skill again afterwards makes the user spin twice again, hitting for 65% and 115% (60% and 110% on larger weapons and Twinblades) of Attack Power respectively.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- The first spin costs 10 points (20 points for larger weapons) of Stamina to perform. The follow-up spin costs 25 points (35 points for larger weapons) of Stamina to perform, 10 points for the first hit and 15 points (25 points for larger weapons) respectively.
- Weapons that use the tight spin/small weapons are Daggers, Straight Swords, Curved Swords, Twinblades, and Axes, while weapons with the sweeping spin/larger weapons are Greatswords, Curved Greatswords, Greataxes, Spears, Great Spears, Halberds, and Reapers.
- 
- Particularly effective on very long weapons like a Pike or Nagakiba, especially since the latter uses the quicker variant.
- For smaller weapons if the first hit lands an enemy player can be locked into the whole 3-hit combo without being able to roll out, making it deal devastating damage.
 - The Nagakiba and its great reach is a very strong combination with this skill.
- Stance damage multipliers varies by weapon size. Smaller weapons deal 290% Stance damage on the first and last hits while the second only deals 90% Stance damage (670% total), while large weapons hit for 230% on the first and last hit and 75% on the second hit (535% total).
 - Throwing Blades Shadow of the Erdtree deal 13.4 Stance damage.
 - Daggers deal 20.1 Stance damage.
 - Spears, Halberds, and Reapers deal 26.75 Stance damage.
 - Straight Swords, Light Greatswords Shadow of the Erdtree, Curved Swords, Backhand Blades Shadow of the Erdtree, Katanas, Twinblades, and Axes deal 33.5 Stance damage.
 - Greatswords, Curved Greatswords, Great Katanas Shadow of the Erdtree, Greataxes, and Great Spears deal 29.425 Stance damage.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Patch 1.12 PvP-only adjustment: Decreased damage.
 - The damage multiplier against other players was lowered from 80% to 70%, an effective 12.5% decrease in damage against other players.
- Patch 1.12 Decreased the status buildup of your weapon when using this skill. Fixed a bug with Spinning Slash Skill that generated poise when used with Twinblades.
 - The Status Effect multiplier was decreased from 100% on each hit (300% build-up in total) to 65% on the first hit, 50% on the second hit, and 70% on the final slam (185% build-up in total).
- Patch 1.07 Increased poise damage against enemies when used with the following weapons: Greatswords, Curved Greatswords, Twinblades, Greataxes, Spears, Great Spears, Halberds, and Reapers.
 - The Stance damage of the first and last hits was increased from 125% to 230%.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown: - Innate skill of the Dragon Halberd.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown:
Call down a blue lightning bolt on the halberd, granting it a Weapon Buff that gives 160 Lightning Attack Power and 80 Frostbite build-up, then spin once, hitting for 105% of Attack Power.

Using the skill again afterwards makes the user spin again before slamming down with the weapon, hitting for 60% and 110% of Attack Power respectively, and sending down a bolt from above with 149 Lightning Attack Power where the head of the weapon hits.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- The first spin costs 21 points of Stamina to perform, while the follow-up takes 36 points of Stamina to do (10 points from the small spin and 26 points from the final slam).
- The Attack Power of the Lightning bolt scales with upgrade level, increasing to 596 at +10.
- If the lightning bolt hits water or a water surface a small area attack with 69 Lightning Attack Power is sent out.
 - This shockwave-in-water scales with upgrade level, increasing to 276 Attack Power at +10.
- The skill can deal up to 26.75 Stance damage with the spins (11.5 for the first spin and final slam each, and 3.75 for the in-between spin) and another 10 Stance damage with the bolt for 36.75 Stance damage in total.
- This skill makes the Dragon Halberd extremely dangerous at low levels since the buff is always at full power and will provide a large amount of extra damage early on.
 - For comparison, a +0 Dragon Halberd at the minimum amount of stat required to wield it has 161 Attack Power while the buff grants another 160 Lightning Attack Power and more or less doubles it.

sections.heading: Trivia

sections.markdown: Skill: Stamp (Upward Cut)** is a Skill in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
- Can be granted to infusable swords, axes, and hammers (except for swords smaller than Greatswords) with the Ash of War: Stamp (Upward Cut).
- Innate skill of many Greatswords: the Banished Knight's Greatsword, Bastard Sword, Fire Knight's Greatsword Shadow of the Erdtree, Flamberge, Forked Greatsword, Greatsword, Iron Greatsword, Knight's Greatsword, Lizard Greatsword Shadow of the Erdtree, Lordsworn's Greatsword, Watchdog's Greatsword, and Zweihander.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown:
Crouches down, ignoring the stagger from the next enemy attack to hit.

Using a heavy attack afterwards causes a slow uppercutting blow, launching human-sized foes, dealing heavy Stance damage, and inflicting damage equal to 215% of the weapon's Attack Power.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- The stomp costs no Stamina (though still requires at least 1 point of Stamina to use) and the heavy follow-up attack costs 50 points of Stamina.
- During the stamp incoming damage is reduced by half.
 - This effectively sets your damage negation to (Current damage negation) + (100 - Current damage negation)/2 or 50 + (Current damage negation)/2.
 - This disappears the same moment the Stagger resistance does, i.e. when the animation for the heavy attack follow-up begins.
- The heavy attack follow-up deals 600% Stance damage.
 - Axes deal 30 Stance damage.
 - Light Greatswords Shadow of the Erdtree, Greatswords, Curved Greatswords, Great Katanas Shadow of the Erdtree, and Greataxes deal 33 Stance damage.
 - Colossal Swords, Flails, and axe-type Colossal Weapons deal 36 Stance damage.
 - Hammers deal 39 Stance damage.
 - Great Hammers deal 42 Stance damage.
 - Hammer-type Colossal Weapons deals 45 Stance damage.
- The Stance damage of the heavy attack follow-up is on par with a charged heavy attack for that weapon type.
- Using a light attack instead of a heavy attack immediately after the crouch will use the second attack of the light attack chain instead of the first one.
 - This attack doesn't cost any FP, unlike the heavy follow-up.
 - This attack is primarily useful for its speed, as it comes out quicker than the heavy attack. While this isn't very useful versus regular enemies, against other players it can be very useful for a mix-up, especially if only the uppercut has been used before.
- While the primary usage would seem to be using the uppercut to launch lesser foe and therefore control their movement, the fact that the initial crouch both resists the stagger of attacks and potentially can duck under high-centered attacks means it can sometimes more easily deliver Stance damage than a charged heavy attack.
 - Especially useful for trading hits with other players, and with special enemies that use the same moveset/skeleton as a player.
- Due to its vertical reach it's capable of catching jumping opponents when they are in mid-air, ignoring the partial invincibility of jumping attacks due to the range.

sections.markdown:

 - Also applies to the Stamp (Sweep) skill.
 - Damage was increased from 200% of Attack Power to 215% of Attack Power.
- Patch 1.08 increased poise value during the active part of the Stamp (Upward Cut) Weapon Art.
 - Also applies to the Stamp (Sweep) skill.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.markdown:
Holding the skill button will make the user swing the weapon at steady pace, alternating between 126% and 119% of weapon Attack Power for the hits (107% and 114% of Attack Power for "Great" weapon types).

Using a light attack when in this stance causes a light slash leading into wide blow to the front, with 52% and 183% of weapon Attack Power (44% and 154% of Attack Power for "Great" weapon types) respectively, while using a heavy attack when in the stance results in backhand slash and an overhead slam that has 52% and 253% weapon Attack Power (44% and 203% of Attack Power for "Great" weapon types) respectively.

- Due to the very stead attack speed it's fairly easy to parry.
- Deals surprisingly heavy Stance damage with the follow-up attacks, with the light attack version dealing between 20 and 26 Stance damage depending on weapon type (equivalent to a jumping heavy attack), and the heavy attack version dealing between 30 and 40 Stance damage depending on weapon type (equivalent to a charged heavy attack).
- Simply using the held version of the skill deals surprising amount of damage, as it both attacks much quicker than normal and consumes low amounts of Stamina per attack. User Poise will also constantly reset, making the user fairly difficult to stagger out of the skill.
 - Very useful against enemies with long staggers upon being Stance broken, such as Dragons, with the repeated strikes often dealing more damage than a Critical Attack. The follow-ups serve as strong endings to such combos, provided they can be timed correctly.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Patch 1.07 shortened the time between various actions and the activation of skills, slightly increased attack power.
 - The swings when the skill button is held had their damage multiplier increased from 120% and 114% (98% and 114% for "Great" weapon types) to 126% and 119% (107% and 114% for "Great" weapon types), damage for the light attack follow-up was increased from 50% and 175% (40% and 140% for "Great" weapon types) to 52% and 183% (44% and 154% for "Great" weapon types), and damage for the heavy attack follow-up was increased from 50% and 230% (40% and 185% for "Great" weapon types) to 52% and 253% (44% and 203% for "Great" weapon types)

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Skill: Lion's Claw** is a Skill in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
- Can be granted to infusable swords, axes, and hammers (except for Daggers and any thrusting sword) with the Ash of War: Lion's Claw.
- Innate skill of the Claymore.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.markdown: Quickly ducks down before leaping forwards with a vertical stuff ending in a slam with the weapon, dealing damage equal to 240% of weapon Attack Power.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 45 points of Stamina to use.
- Damage is boosted by 10% when Freyja's Greatsword Shadow of the Erdtree is held in either active hand.
 - Note that Lion's Claw doesn't necessarily need to be equipped on that weapon to gain the damage bonus.
- Deals 600% Stance damage.
 - Straight Swords, Curved Swords, Katanas, Twinblades, and Axes deal 30 Stance damage.
 - Light Greatswords Shadow of the Erdtree, Greatswords, Curved Greatswords, Great Katanas Shadow of the Erdtree, and Greataxes deal 33 Stance damage.
 - Colossal Swords, Flails, and axe-type Colossal Weapons deal 36 Stance damage.
 - Hammers deal 39 Stance damage.
 - Great Hammers deal 42 Stance damage.
 - Hammer-type Colossal Weapons deals 45 Stance damage.
- Grants heavy hyperarmor when mid-air, effectively making the skill almost impossible to interrupt when leaping.
- Deals heavy Stance damage, on par with a charged heavy attack for that weapon type.
 - Just 2-4 uses is enough to break the Stance of most bosses.
- An excellent skill due to having a quick start-up time and good reach in combination with solid damage and Stance damage.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown: - Patch 1.04 increased cast speed and decreased recovery time.

sections.heading: See also

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Skill: Cragblade** is a Skill in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown: - Can be granted to infusable melee weapons of any type (except for Whips) with the Ash of War: Cragblade.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown:
User slams their weapon into the ground, dealing damage equal to 100% of weapon Attack Power, before pulling it out to deal damage equal to 80% of weapon Attack Power and granting a Weapon Buff.

The buff lasts for 60 seconds and increases Physical damage by 15%, damage to Poise and Stance by 10%, and Stamina damage against blocking opponents by 50%.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 40 points of Stamina to use, divided up as 20 points of Stamina for the slam and another 20 points for the pull.
- Since this is a Weapon Buff it means that it won't stack with other Weapon Buffs such as Fire Grease.
- The slam and the subsequent pull both count as attacks, if very short-ranged ones, and can be parried.
 - The slam deals damage equal to 100% of weapon Attack Power and the pull deals damage equal to 80% of weapon Attack Power.
- An easy-to-use and widely applicable skill for Physical-damage dependent attackers, since it's relatively easy to set-and-forget and only occasionally has to be re-used to re-apply the buff. It also just generally boosts combat performance, without the user having to think much about using it.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Patch 1.07 extended effect duration, increased attack power, poise damage and stamina attack power against guarding enemies.
 - Duration was increased from 30 seconds to 60 seconds, and attack power bonus was increased from 10% to 15%, Poise/Stance damage bonus was increased from 10% to 20%, and Stamina damage against blocking opponents was increased from 20% to 50%.
- Patch 1.08 reduced the poise damage of the Cragblade Weapon Art.
 - Poise/Stance damage bonus was reduced back down from 20% to 10%.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Skill: Kick** is a Skill in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
- Can be granted to infusable melee weapons of any type with the Ash of War: Kick
- Innate skill of the Arbalest, Crepus's Black-Key Crossbow, Full Moon Crossbow, Hammer, Hand Ballista, Heavy Crossbow, Hoslow's Petal Whip, Jar Cannon, Light Crossbow, Mace, Monk's Flamemace, Morning Star, Pulley Crossbow, Rabbath's CannonShadow of the Erdtree, Short Sword, Soldier's Crossbow, Spread CrossbowShadow of the Erdtree, Stone Club, Thorned Whip, Urumi, Warpick, and Whip.
- This is also the innate skill of The Tarnished's own empty fists.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.markdown: Kicks with one foot, causing an attack with a low 30 base Strike Attack Power, staggering foes, and breaking their guard by dealing 999 damage to the Stamina of guarding opponents.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 16 points of Stamina to use.
- Does NOT appear to be boosted by the Shattered Stone Talisman.
- Actually a "bullet"-type Skill, meaning its (admittedly pretty poor) damage scales entirely from weapon upgrade level and Strength.
 - It's not really worth trying to make this skill deal damage, as even when used on a weapon with a Heavy affinity for increased scaling and 80 Strength will have at most 180 Attack Power or so, and this is before enemy flat defences are applied and reduce the damage even further.
- Can break the guard of pretty much any blocking enemy, even Crucible Knights.
 - Somewhat more limited effectiveness against player Greatshields as the short reach makes it harder to use.
- Deals light Stance damage, 6, about as much as a Hammers light attack.
- This skill's effect can mostly be replicated by either simply attacking with the Hammer Talisman equipped, which is simpler than equipping this skill on a weapon or leaving the right-hand and left-hand skill slots empty and can have a fair bit more range, but takes up a Talisman slot and isn't a guaranteed guard break.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Patch 1.07 increased poise damage and stamina attack power against guarding enemies.
 - The damage to the Stamina of guarding opponents was increased from 350 to 999.

sections.heading: See also

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Skill: Endure** is a Skill in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
- Can be granted to infusable melee weapons of any type with the Ash of War: Endure.
- Innate skill of the Blacksteel GreathammerShadow of the Erdtree, Bloodfiend's ArmShadow of the Erdtree, Caestus, Dragon Greatclaw, Duelist Greataxe, Giant-Crusher, Golem FistShadow of the Erdtree, Great Mace, Great Stars, Iron Ball (though it has Ash of War: Braggart's Roar equipped, overriding the skill), Pickaxe, Rotten Greataxe, Smithscript GreathammerShadow of the Erdtree, Spiked Caestus, and Star Fist,

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown: Briefly raises the weapon and hold still. For 3 seconds Poise is greatly increased, Damage Negation is increased by a flat 45%, and user has Tier 1 Deflection against weapons.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Since the boost to Poise that this Skill grants lasts an additional 2 seconds after the animation has ended, the player can tank damage to use healing flasks or trade hits without the risk of getting stunned.
 - Putting this on a light weapon such as a Dagger or Caestus gives a player a convenient tool for more easily using items and skills in tight situations.
 - This Poise boost doesn't prevent stagger from headshots and attacks that launch you into the air.
- Tier 1 Deflection means that certain one-handed attacks (mostly regular light attacks) from Daggers, Thrusting Swords, Katanas, Twinblades, Spears, Reapers, Claws, and Torches causes the attacker hitstun.
 - This is most likely also true for Throwing BladesShadow of the Erdtree, Backhand BladesShadow of the Erdtree, and Beast ClawsShadow of the Erdtree weapon types, but this needs checking.
- Larger weapons (Greatswords, Colossal Swords, Greataxes, Great Hammers, and Colossal Weapons) have a slower version of the initial stance, taking roughly 1.5-2 seconds, making this skill harder to use for them.
 - This is most likely also shared with the Great KatanasShadow of the Erdtree weapon type, but this needs checking.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Patch 1.07 extended effect duration, added an effect that prevents staggers caused by blood loss and frostbite status effects, reduced the time between skill activation and being able to perform actions other than attacking.
 - Duration increased from 3 seconds to 5 seconds.
- Patch 1.07.1 shortened effect duration. Adjustments made in patch 1.07 had a greater impact on the game balance than expected.
 - Duration was lowered back down again, from 5 seconds to 3 seconds.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Skill: Ground Slam** is a Skill in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown: Can be granted to infusable melee weapons of any type with the Ash of War: Ground Slam.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown: Slightly crouches down before jumping up into the air and then lands to with base 264 Strike Attack Power on a direct hit and cause shockwave for another 175 base Standard Attack Power.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 40 points of Stamina to perform.
- As a bullet-type skill the Attack Power scales with the weapon's upgrade level and the user's Strength.
 - Strength-scaling is greatly increased if the weapon has a Heavy affinity, slightly increased if it has a Fire affinity, and somewhat increased on a Quality, Cold, Poison, or Blood affinity, and greatly decreased if the weapon has a Keen, Lightning, Magic, or Occult affinity.
 - Attack Power is always at least 1056 for a direct hit and 700 for the shockwave for a weapon at maximum upgrade level.
 - A Quality, Cold, Poison, or Blood affinity and 45 Strength gives the direct hit 1291 Attack Power and the shockwave 856 Attack Power, while a Fire affinity and either 45 or 80 Strength gives respectively the direct hit either 1316 Attack Power or 1430 Attack Power and the shockwave either 872 Attack Power or 948 Attack Power, and a Heavy affinity and either 45 or 80 Strength gives respectively the direct hit either 1403 Attack Power or 1555 Attack Power and the shockwave either 930 Attack Power or 1031 Attack Power.
- User gains hyperarmor when in mid-air, making it very difficult to knock them out of the skill.
 - Do note that it doesn't grant any invincibility frames, unlike a jump (which grants those from the waist down), meaning that if an attack isn't completely and physically avoided damage may still be taken more often than normal.
- Deals surprisingly heavy Stance damage, 15 on the landing hit and 30 on the following shockwave. For comparison, a Great Hammer's charged heavy attack deals 40 Stance damage and a hammer-type Colossal Weapon's charged heavy attack deals 42 Stance damage.
- Will flatten human-sized enemies if they are hit directly.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Patch 1.07 reduced the time between using the skill and being able to roll, increased attack power.
 - Base Attack Power for the direct hit was increased from 240 to 264 and base Attack Power for the shockwave was increased from 160 to 175.

sections.heading: See also
sections.markdown:
- Skill: Golden Slam, a Holy variant of this skill
- Unique Skill: Erdtree Slam, a stronger Holy variant of this skill

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Skill: Earthshaker** is a Skill in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown: - Can be granted to infusable axes, hammers, and spears of great-size and larger as well as Colossal Swords with the Ash of War: Earthshaker.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown:
Slam weapon head first into the ground, dealing damage equal to 100% of weapon Attack Power, before causing a shockwave all around the user with 120 base Standard Attack Power.

Using a heavy attack afterwards causes the user spin around to lunge forward while sweeping the weapon in front of them, dealing damage equal to 140% of weapon Attack Power.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- The initial slam costs 25 points of Stamina to perform, the shockwave costs another 8 points of Stamina, and the follow-up attack costs 35 points of Stamina to do.
- Since the initial slam down into the ground is an attack it's capable of interrupting very close foes.
- The initial slam and the follow-up attack scales with the used weapon's Attack Power, while the shockwave is a bullet-type and as such scales with the weapon's upgrade level and the user's Strength.
 - Strength-scaling for the shockwave is greatly increased if the weapon has a Heavy affinity, slightly increased if it has a Fire affinity, and somewhat increased on a Quality, Cold, Poison, or Blood affinity, and greatly decreased if the weapon has a Keen, Lightning, Magic, or Occult affinity.
 - Attack Power of the shockwave is always at least 480 for a weapon at maximum upgrade level.
 - A Quality, Cold, Poison, or Blood affinity and 45 Strength gives the shockwave 587 Attack Power, while a Fire affinity and either 45 or 80 Strength gives respectively 598 Attack Power or 650 Attack Power, and a Heavy affinity and either 45 or 80 Strength gives respectively 638 Attack Power or 707 Attack Power.
 - This skill is still fairly usable on those affinities, as while the shockwave will see a roughly 25% penalty to Attack Power on a low-Strength build with a weakening affinity compared to a high-Strength build with a Heavy affinity the direct weapon hits still work well.
- The follow-up can launch human-sized foes backwards.
- The follow-up can actually be delayed a fair bit, useful against other players when waiting out their rolls or simply using it after they would've expected you to be unable to use it.

sections.heading: See also
sections.markdown:

- Skill: Golden Land, essentially a Holy-based variant of this skill with added projectiles

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Skill: Hoarah Loux's Earthshaker** is a Skill in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown: - Can be granted to infusible melee weapons of any type with Ash of War: Hoarah Loux's Earthshaker.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown:
Let loose a staggering, 0 damage roar before slamming down to send out a shockwave with 220 Standard Attack Power.

Using the skill again causes another slam to send out a shockwave with 250 Standard Attack Power.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 25 points of Stamina per slam (50 total if both are used).
- Deals 15 Stance damage with the first part of the roar and 1 Stance damage for the second and third parts of the roar, while each slam deals 20 Stance, for a total Stance damage of 57 if the entire skills is used and hits.
- The roar is actually 3 separate 0 damage hits.
 - Each hit of the roar still causes damage to the Stamina of guarding enemies, and also counts as a hit for the purpose of gaining the Attack Power buff from the Winged Sword Insignias. If all 3 hits land on a single target this means that 1 tier of said attack boost is gained and will be applied to the slam-shockwaves. If the roars hit more than 1 target the boost can potentially be even stronger.
- Since the shockwaves are ground-bound they can be jumped over.
- This is a bullet-type skill so the damage scales with the weapon's upgrade level and the user's Strength.
 - Strength-scaling is greatly increased if the weapon has a Heavy affinity, slightly increased if it has a Fire affinity, and somewhat increased on a Cold, Poison, or Blood affinity, and greatly decreased if the weapon has a Keen, Lightning, Magic, or Occult affinity.
 - Attack Power of the roar is always at least 880 for the first shockwave and 1000 for the second shockwave for a weapon at maximum upgrade level.
 - A Cold, Poison, or Blood affinity and 45 Strength gives the shockwaves 1076 and 1223 Attack Power respectively, while a Fire affinity and either 45 or 80 Strength gives 1097 respectively 1192 Attack Power for the first shockwave and 1246 respectively 1354 Attack Power on the second shockwave, and a Heavy affinity and either 45 or 80 Strength gives 1169 respectively 1296 Attack Power for the first shockwave and 1328 respectively 1473 Attack Power for the second shockwave.
- Deals 20% less damage against players.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Patch 1.05 fixed a bug in which a status effect was applied when using the "Hoarah Loux's Earthshaker" skill.
- Patch 1.04 increased cast speed. Increased cast speed on follow up input, decreased recovery time.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Skill: War Cry** is a Skill in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
- Can be granted to any infusable melee weapon (except for small weapons, thrusting swords, and Whips) with the Ash of War: War Cry.
- Innate skill of several Axes (Highland Axe, Messmer Soldier's Axe Shadow of the Erdtree, and Warped Axe) and Greataxes (Crescent Moon Axe, Executioner's Greataxe, Gargoyle's Black Axe, Gargoyle's Great Axe, and Longhaft Axe).

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown:
Roar to gain a Weapon Buff that increases the weapon's Physical Attack Power by 7.5% and adds 0.05 to its Strength-scaling for 40 seconds.

When the Weapon Buff is active, regular heavy attacks are turned into overhead slam with 135% Attack Power (145% if two-handed), with a second regular heavy attack being an upward slash with the same Attack Power. For Fists-sized weapons their two-handed regular heavy attacks become two slams with 100% Attack Power each.

If a charged heavy attack instead is performed, it's preceded by a charge that hits with 0 Attack Power twice to stagger and then the attack has is an overhead slam with 175% Attack Power (185% if two-handed), and a second charged heavy attack is preceded by a charge that hits with 0 Attack Power once and the attack is another overhead slam with 178% Attack Power (188% if two-handed). For Fists-sized weapons their two-handed charged heavy attacks become two slams with 125% Attack Power each for the first charged heavy attack and 130% Attack Power for the second one.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Best for large, high Attack Power weapons (such as Colossal Swords and Colossal Weapons) that can take advantage the most of the high multipliers.
- The initial roar costs 20 points of Stamina. The cost for the changed heavy attack depends on the weapon's type, whether or not the attack is charged, and whether or not the weapon is being two-handed or not: 20-40 points for one-handed reguar heavy attacks (24-48 points if two-handed) and 35-55 points for one-handed charged heavy attacks (40-66 points if two-handed).
 - For Fists, Hand-to-Hand Shadow of the Erdtree, Claws, and Beast Claws Shadow of the Erdtree one-handed regular heavy attacks cost 20 points of Stamina (15+15 points if two-handed) and one-handed charged heavy attacks for 35 points of Stamina (20+20 points if two-handed).
 - For Straight Swords, Light Greatswords Shadow of the Erdtree, Curved Swords, Katanas, Great Katanas Shadow of the Erdtree, Twinblades, Axes, Hammers, and Flails one-handed regular heavy attacks cost 30 points of Stamina (36 points if two-handed) and one-handed charged heavy attacks for 45 points of Stamina (54 points if two-handed).
 - For Greatswords, Curved Greatswords, Spears, Halberds, and Reapers one-handed regular heavy attacks cost 35 points of Stamina (42 points if two-handed) and one-handed charged heavy attacks for 50 points of Stamina (60 points if two-handed).
 - For Great Hammers one-handed regular heavy attacks cost 37 points of Stamina (45 points if two-handed) and one-handed charged heavy attacks for 52 points of Stamina (63 points if two-handed).
 - For Greataxes and Great Spears one-handed regular heavy attacks cost 38 points of Stamina (46 points if two-handed) and one-handed charged heavy attacks for 53 points of Stamina (64 points if two-handed).
 - For Colossal Swords and Colossal Weapons one-handed regular heavy attacks cost 40 points of Stamina on the first attack and 45 points on the second attack (48 points on first and 54 points on second if two-handed) and one-handed charged heavy attacks for 55 points of Stamina (66 points if two-handed).
- The changed heavy attack is different between slashing weapons, spears, and fist-sized weapons. When the heavy attack is charged the attack will be preceded by a short, staggering charge.
 - For Straight Swords, Light Greatswords Shadow of the Erdtree, Greatswords, Colossal Swords, Curved Swords, Curved Greatswords, Katanas, Great Katanas Shadow of the Erdtree, Axes, Greataxes, Hammers, Flails, Great Hammers, Colossal Weapons, and Reapers the first attack is an overhead slam while the second attack is an upwards cut. Speed varies slightly by the size of the weapon type.
 - For Twinblades the first attack is a jumping forwards stab while the second attack is an upwards cut.
 - For Spears, Great Spears, and Halberds the first attack is a jumping forwards stab while the second attack is another thrust.
 - For Fists, Hand-to-Hand Shadow of the Erdtree, Claws, and Beast Claws Shadow of the Erdtree the first attack is an overhead slam while the second attack is a spinning uppercut.
- For all one-handed weapons the Stance damage multipliers are the same, with the regular heavy attack dealing 200% Stance damage and the charged heavy attack dealing 600% Stance damage. Two-handed fist-sized weapons, however, deal 120% Stance damage per hit (240% in total) with regular heavy attacks, while charged heavy attacks deal 360% Stance damage per hit (720% in total) with the first attack and 480% Stance damage (960% in total) with the second attack.
 - For all weapons that aren't fist-sized, two-handing the weapon increases the Stance damage by 20% for the regular heavy attacks by 20% and by 10% for the charged heavy attacks.
 - Hand-to-Hand Shadow of the Erdtree, Claws, and Beast Claws Shadow of the Erdtree deal 8 Stance damage with one-handed regular heavy attacks (9.6 Stance damage in total if two-handed) and 24 Stance damage with one-handed charged heavy attacks (28.8 Stance damage in total with the first one and 38.4 Stance damage in total with the second one if two-handed).
 - Fists deal 10 Stance damage with one-handed regular heavy attacks (12 Stance damage in total if two-handed) and 30 Stance damage with one-handed charged heavy attacks (36 Stance damage in total with the first one and 48 Stance damage in total with the second one if two-handed).
 - Straight Swords, Curved Swords, Katanas, Twinblades, Axes, Spears, Halberds, and Reapers deal 10 Stance damage with one-handed regular heavy attacks (12 Stance damage if two-handed) and 30 Stance damage with one-handed charged heavy attacks (33 Stance damage if two-handed).
 - Light Greatswords Shadow of the Erdtree, Greatswords, Curved Greatswords, Greataxes, and Great Spears deal 11 Stance damage with one-handed regular heavy attacks (13.2 Stance damage if two-handed) and 33 Stance damage with one-handed charged heavy attacks (36.3 Stance damage if two-handed).
 - Colossal Swords, Flails, and axe-type Colossal Weapons deal 12 Stance damage with one-handed regular heavy attacks (14.4 Stance damage if two-handed) and 36 Stance damage with one-handed charged heavy attacks (39.6 Stance damage if two-handed).
 - Hammers deal 13 Stance damage with one-handed regular heavy attacks (15.6 Stance damage if two-handed) and 39 Stance damage with one-handed charged heavy attacks (42.9 Stance damage if two-handed).
 - Great Hammers deal 14 Stance damage with one-handed regular heavy attacks (16.8 Stance damage if two-handed) and 42 Stance damage with one-handed charged heavy attacks (46.2 Stance damage if two-handed).
 - Hammer-type Colossal Weapons deal 15 Stance damage with one-handed regular heavy attacks (18 Stance damage if two-handed) and 45 Stance damage with one-handed charged heavy attacks (49.5 Stance damage if two-handed).
- The charged heavy attacks used when under the effect of War Cry have a higher than usual Status Effects multiplier, as most of them inflict 200% of the Status Effect per hit.
 - Colossal Swords and Colossal Weapons have 300% Status Effect build-up.
 - Two-handed Fists, Hand-to-Hand Shadow of the Erdtree, Claws, and Beast Claws Shadow of the Erdtree have 150% Status Effect build-up on each of the two hits.
- The added Strength-scaling is additive and is most beneficial for Heavy Affinity and Fire Affinity weapons, as they already have strong Strength-scaling will most likely be used for builds built around that stat.
 - This effectively adds up 5% extra Attack Power compared to Base Attack Power, though it will be lower due to Weapon Scaling (3.125% extra at 45 Strength and 4.5% extra at 80 Strength).
 - Example: a +25 Fire Affinity Longsword has 0.73 (C) Strength-scaling. After using War Cry that scaling will have improved to 0.78 (C).
- Though this is a skill, the follow-up heavy attacks are not boosted by the Warrior Jar Shards. Attack Power of both the regular and charged heavy attack follow-up is however increased by 15% by the Roar Medallion and by 10% if a Highland Axe is held in an active hand slot, and the charged heavy attack follow-up has its Attack Power increased by 10% by the Axe Talisman.
- The changed heavy attacks are rather predictable for parries due to their slow speed, unless the weapon type (such as Flails) is unparriable.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Patch 1.07 Extended effect duration. Reduced the delay between the end of various actions (such as using items or attack animations) and being able to perform the skill. The power of strong attacks during the duration of the effect has been increased when using the following weapons: Straight Sword / Curved Sword / Katana / Axe / Hammer / Flail / Spear / Great Spear / Halberd / Reaper / Fist (one-handed) / Claw (one-handed).
 - The duration of the Weapon Buff was extended from 20 seconds to 40 seconds.
- Patch 1.05: Fixed a bug in the "War Cry" skill where the effect was applied to a weapon that was not the target of the skill. Fixed a bug where recovery time for some actions of the "Barbaric Roar", "War Cry", and "Troll's Roar" was longer than expected.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Skill: Barbaric Roar** is a Skill in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
- Can be granted to any infusable weapon through Ash of War: Barbaric Roar.
- Default skill on the Butchering Knife, Club, Curved Club, Curved Great Club, Rusted Anchor, and Spiked Club weapons.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown:
Grants a Weapon Buff for 40 seconds upon use, increasing damage by roughly 10%.

As long as this buff remains active the regular heavy and charged heavy attacks are changed to a 3-hit combo, which can then be followed by either a single hit or a 2-hit combo depending on the weapon type.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Although this Skill functions similarly to War Cry, the new heavy attack animations are different.
- Though it is a Weapon Buff, its visual effect is more akin to a Body Buff, being red rising lines around the user's body.
- New attacks resemble the original moveset of the weapon used, meaning most weapons will perform heavy slashing or smashing attacks.
 - The exception to this is the various polearms (Spears, Halberds, and Great Spears) as well as the Twinblades final follow-up attack, which instead are thrusts.
- The Roar Medallion and the Highland Axe can be worn to further increase the damage of the two follow-up attack combos.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Skill: Braggart's Roar** is a Skill in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Skill: Troll's Roar** is a Skill in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
- Can granted to infusable large and colossal swords, axes, and hammers with the Ash of War: Troll's Roar.
- Default skill on the Troll's Golden Sword, Troll's Hammer and Troll Knight's Sword.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown:
Slowly step forward and let loose a roar with 195 base Strike Attack Power (155 base Standard Attack Power for targets further out) to hit enemies around you.

Use a heavy attack to follow-up with a slow, overhead slam with Attack Power equal to 180% of the weapon's own.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- The roar costs 30 points of Stamina while the follow-up heavy attack costs 40 points of Stamina.
- The Attack Power of both the roar and the follow-up heavy attack is boosted by 15% if the Roar Medallion is worn.
- The Attack Power of both the roar and the follow-up heavy attack is boosted by 10% if a Highland Axe is held in one of a character's active hand slots (this boost remains active even if the weapon with Troll's Roar is two-handed).
- The roar is a bullet-type skill so its Attack Power scales with the weapon's upgrade level and the user's Strength.
 - Strength-scaling is greatly increased if the weapon has a Heavy Affinity, slightly increased if it has a Fire Affinity, and somewhat increased on a Quality, Cold, Poison, or Blood Affinity, and greatly decreased if the weapon has a Keen, Lightning, Magic, or Occult Affinity.
 - Since the Troll's Hammer counts as a Standard affinity weapon despite its ample Strength-scaling and being unable to change the skill, making its roar deal substantially less damage than a Heavy affinity weapon at equivalent levels of Strength (15% less Attack Power at 80 Strength) while the Troll Knight's Sword has somewhat improved Strength-scaling due to being a Somber weapon with decent Strength-scaling at +0.
 - Attack Power of the roar is always at least 780 (620 for more distant targets) for a weapon at maximum upgrade level.
 - A Quality, Cold, Poison, or Blood affinity and 45 Strength gives the roar 954 Attack Power (758 against distant targets), while a Fire affinity and either 45 or 80 Strength gives respectively 972 Attack Power (773 against distant targets) or 1056 Attack Power (840 against distant targets), and a Heavy affinity and either 45 or 80 Strength gives respectively 1036 Attack Power (823 against distant targets) or 1149 Attack Power (913 against distant targets).
 - The Troll's Hammer's roar has 917 Attack Power (729 against distant targets) at 45 Strength and 977 Attack Power (777 against distant targets), while the Troll Knight's Sword's roar has 1076 Attack Power (855 against distant targets) at 45 Strength and 1206 Attack Power (959 against distant targets).
- The roar deals 40 Stance damage (only 9 Stance damage against more distant targets) and the follow-up deals either 33 Stance damage (Greatswords, Heavy Thrusting Swords, Curved Greatswords, and Greataxes), 36 Stance damage (Colossal Swords and non-hammer Colossal Weapons), 42 Stance damage (Great Hammers), or 45 Stance damage (hammer Colossal Weapons).
- Only the roar costs FP to perform, with the follow-up heavy attack having no FP cost.
- The roar throws back enemies that are hit.
- The follow-up heavy attack has an unusually high modifier of 180% for Status Effects, whereas most Skills and weapon attacks has a modifier of 100% or lower.
- Hits quite hard but is very slow and as such hard to hit with, the follow-up even more so since it has a smaller hitbox.
 - Especially hard to use against other players since it's so slow, though that slowness can also bait them to roll early and get caught by either the roar or follow-up attack.
 - The roar has a tendency to throw smaller enemies out of reach for the follow-up, so it can be better to reserve said follow-up for when an enemy is knocked back into a closeby wall or obstacle, or for when an enemy's Stance is broken.
 - Consider using a light attack as a follow-up instead, as it will come out quicker and can be surprising if used only occasionally against other players.
- Deals 20% less damage against other players.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Skill: Impaling Thrust** is a Skill in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
- Can be granted to infusable weapons capable of making thrusting attacks (except for Colossal Swords) with the Ash of War: Impaling Thrust.
 - Note that while two Fists has Impaling Thrust as their innate skill, they cannot equip the Ash of War and as such can only use the skill with a Standard affinity.
- Innate skill of many Thrusting Swords, Heavy Thrusting Swords, Spears, and Fists.
 - Thrusting Swords: Antspur Rapier, Carian Sorcery Sword Shadow of the Erdtree, Cleanrot Knight's Sword, Estoc, Frozen Needle, Noble's Estoc, and Rapier.
 - Heavy Thrusting Swords: Godskin Stitcher, Great Épée, Queelign's Greatsword Shadow of the Erdtree, and Sword Lance Shadow of the Erdtree.
 - Spears Clayman's Harpoon, Cross-Naginata, Crystal Spear, Partisan, Short Spear, Smithscript Spear Shadow of the Erdtree, Spear, Spiked Spear, and Swift Spear Shadow of the Erdtree.
 - Fists (not compatible with the Ash of War): Katar and Pata Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown: Lunge forward with a attack that always deals Pierce damage, hits for 187% Attack Power, and ignores 85% of Guarded Damage Negation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 40 point of Stamina to use.
 - The version found on the Carian Sorcery Sword Shadow of the Erdtree costs slightly less to perform, at 39 points of Stamina.
- The block-piercing effect effectively scales with how high the Guard Damage Negation of an opponent's blocking implement is. For a 100% Guard Damage Negation rate only 1-1*0.85=0.15=15% damage will be blocked while a 50% Guarded Damage Negation rate will let 0.5-0.5*0.85=0.075=7.5% damage will be blocked.
 - Effectively, if x is the blocking implement's Guarded Damage Negation then the formular x*(1-0.85)=0.15*x can be applied to know how much damage will be blocked when using Impaling Thrust (or 1-0.15*x for how large a fraction of the damage of Impaling Thrust will go through).
- The effective damage against a Guarding opponent can become slightly lower than 85% of the damage against a non-Guarding opponent if the decrease lowers the effective Attack Power compared to the opponent's defense.
- The Stance damage multiplier per hit is 600%, the same as with Lion's Claw. This is the same amount of Stance damage as a one-handed charged heavy attack for that weapon type (except for Throwing Blades, where the Stance damage is doubled compared to a one-handed charged heavy attack).
 - Throwing Blades Shadow of the Erdtree deal 12 Stance damage.
 - Daggers and Claws deal 18 Stance damage.
 - Thrusting Swords deal 24 Stance damage.
 - Straight Swords, Katanas, Twinblades, Spears, Halberds, and Fists deal 30 Stance damage.
 - Light Greatswords Shadow of the Erdtree, Greatswords, Heavy Thrusting Swords, Great Katanas Shadow of the Erdtree, and Great Spears deal 33 Stance damage.
- Compared with Piercing Fang: lower FP cost (9 vs 16), lower Attack Power modifier (187% vs 212%), lower Guard-piercing (85% vs 100%), shorter lunge distance, quicker cast, and same Stance damage multiplier (600%).
- Due to the fairly long delay this skill is fairly easy to recognize and parry for other players.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Patch 1.07 increased motion speed and attack power, reduced the delay between the end of various actions (such as using items or attack animations) and being able to perform the skill, and reduced the timing between the end of the skill and being able to attack and to roll.
 - Increased the Attack Power from 170% to 187%.
 - The other changed increased the speed of the lunge, how early the skill can be used, and the aftercast duration of the skill where nothing else can be done.

sections.heading: See also
sections.markdown:
- Skill: Piercing Fang, a similar, slower skill with more damage and guard-piercing
- Skill: Giant Hunt, a thrusting skill that exchanges guard-piercing for launching foes into the air

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown:
Rotates around and stab forward with 99% Attack Power, then thrust twice more for 57% Attack Power on each hit, and finally inflict a piercing blow with 115% Attack Power.

sections.heading: Notes

- Compared to Skill: Blood Tax this skill costs less FP (7 vs 16), deals has more Attack Power in total (328% vs 286%), costs less Stamina (33 points vs 45 points), and has the same total amount of Status Effect build-up (200%), in exchange for Blood Tax also restoring HP on hit (10% of maximum HP + 120 in total).
- Works quite well with long weapons such as Halberds since it gives a good amount of reach and lets the user stagger human-sized foes, while also breaking Stance fairly well.
- Easily parried since all 4 separate hits can be parried.
- Deals 200% Stance damage with the first thrust, then 40% Stance damage on the two middle thrusts and 100% Stance damage on the final stab (80% Stance damage with the final stab for Daggers) for 380% Stance damage in total (360% in total for Daggers).

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown:
Make two horisontal slashes with 92% and 105% Attack Power.

Using the skill again makes the user spin around before making another three horisontal slashes, hitting with 84%, 86%, and 115% Attack Power respectively.

Using the skill a third time leads to final, strong overhead slash with 145% Attack Power.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 6 FP on the first input and then 3 FP each for the other two inputs (12 FP in total).
- Each slash from the first two inputs cost 14 points of Stamina each while the final attack costs 20 points of Stamina (90 points in total for the whole skill).
 - For larger weapons the first five slash take 16 points each while the final one needs 24 points (104 points of Stamina in total for the whole skill).
 - While it's very Stamina-hungry overall, only 1 point of Stamina is needed to start each sequence. This means only 29 points of Stamina is needed to use the second input (33 points for larger weapons) and 71 points for the final input (81 points for larger weapons). Be wary that this will leave you without any Stamina for a few seconds.
- Larger weapons (Greatswords, Curved Greatswords, Great Katanas, Twinblades, Halberds, and Reapers) have a slower variant of this skill, with more of a delay between each input's attack sequence.
- Deals 75% Stance damage on the first, third, and fourth slash, 100% Stance damage on the second and fifth slash, and 200% Stance damage on the final, sixth attack (625% Stance damage in total).
 - Throwing Blades deal 12.5 Stance damage in total.
 - Daggers deal 18.75 Stance damage in total.
 - Straight Swords, Curved Swords, Katanas, and Twinblades deal 31.25 Stance damage in total.
 - Light Greatswords , Greatswords, Curved Greatswords, Great Katanas , Halberds, and Reapers deal 34.375 Stance damage in total.
- Deals 525% of the weapon's innate Status Effect build-up over the course of the entire skill (175% on the first input, 250% on the second input, and 100% on the third input).
- Very parriable, as each of the six separate hits are parriable.
- Very flexible in its usage. The first input is quite quick and easy to use, the second input is strong but very long, and the third input is by far the strongest per hit but requires using the other two parts beforehand.

sections.markdown: Skill: Unsheathe** is a Skill in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
- Can be granted to infusable Katanas with the Ash of War: Unsheathe.
 - Since all infusable Katanas already have Unsheathe as their innate skill, the purpose of this is purely to change their Affinity.
- Innate skill of the Nagakiba and Uchigatana.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown:
Using and holding the skill places the Katana in its sheath and the user in a stance, while the user's Stamina regeneration rate and movement speed is greatly decreased.

Using a light attack while in this Stance makes the user dash forward slightly and make a horizontal slash with 190% Attack Power.

Using a heavy attack while in this Stance makes the user step forward and perform a heavy overhead slash with 245% Attack Power.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- The Stance costs no points of Stamina. The light attack follow-up costs 24 points of Stamina while the heavy attack follow-up costs 40 points of Stamina.
 - The Stance costs no points of FP. The light attack follow-up costs 10 points of FP while the heavy attack follow-up costs 15 points of FP.
- The light attack follow-up deals 300% Stance damage while the heavy attack follow-up one deals 600% Stance damage.
 - This means the light attack follow-up deals 15 Stance damage while the heavy attack follow-up deals 30 Stance damage.
- The Rellana's Cameo grants a 45% boost to Attack Power to the follow-up attacks if the Stance is held for at least a second.
- This is an extremely strong skill in PvE, primarily due to how quick and damaging the heavy attack follow-up is and due to it dealing 30 Stance damage, on par with a charged heavy attack, and thus being able to break most enemies' Stance in 3-4 hits.
- The Stance can be cancelled without using a follow-up attack.

sections.heading: Summary

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
- Can be granted to any infusable melee weapon with the Ash of War: Quickstep.
- Innate skill of many Daggers and Claws, and a few Axes.
 - Daggers: Bloodstained Dagger, Celebrant's Sickle, Cinquedea, Crystal Knife, Dagger, Erdsteel Dagger, Fire Knight's Shortsword Shadow of the Erdtree, Great Knife, Ivory Sickle, Miséricorde, and Wakizashi.

sections.heading: Basics
sections.markdown:
The Player Character dashes quickly in any direction. This dash has invincibility frames (i-frames), the amount of said i-frames depends on the player's Equip Load. The distance and i-frame-count gradually decreases the more Quickstep is used repeatedly in quick succession.

While quickstep is omnidirectional, it mainly uses the four primary directions (left, right, forward, backward) as a base for it's movement and should the player follow up a step with a normal, non-strong attack, what attack-animation is used depends on which of these base-directions are used.
- Forward: triggers the Rolling Attack, with it's fast windup, but short reach.
- Left, Right and Backwards: triggers the Backstep Attack, with it's ability to quickly close distances.

Quickstep can also be used to quickly move through waist-deep waters and swamps.

sections.heading: Advanced
sections.markdown:
Inexperienced users may be thrown off from quickstep's base-directional nature during especially hectic fights, (particularly when implementing both locked-on and locked-off play) it is possible to take advantage of the different directional dashing animations by intentionally aiming them in unintended directions.

Such as the reverse-quickstep, with it's ability to quickly position the player directly behind the enemy or close even further distances, which can be performed with these inputs:

sections.heading: Advanced
sections.markdown: If the player can time and space their reverse-quickstep correctly they may even be able to put themselves in the perfect position for a backstab against humanoid opponents. This is one of the fastest, safest and most consistent ways a player can weave in backstabs against an aggressive opponent in PvP.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 12 points of Stamina per use.
- If used without meeting the stat requirements of the weapon this skill costs no FP, which is useful for traveling in environments where you can't run.
- Compared to Skill: Bloodhound's Step this skill costs less FP (3 vs 5) in exchange for traveling a shorter distance and not becoming partially invisible during its use.

sections.heading: Trivia

- Patch 1.06: Shortened the activation interval when using “Quick Step” skill in succession, increasing its ability to circle around the enemy when locked-on and add the changes below: Reduced performance when used continuously, Increased travel distance when on light equip load.
 - Quickstep is incorrectly referred to as "Quick Step" in this update.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Skill: Bloodhound's Step** is a Skill in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
- Can be granted to any infusable melee weapon or thrusting shield with the Ash of War: Bloodhound's Step.
- Innate skill of the Bloodhound Claws.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown: Turn invisible while dashing in the character's current direction (forwards by default), granting 16 i-frames (0.53 seconds) (14 i-frames (0.47 seconds) on follow-up uses).

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 12 points of Stamina.
- The dodging functions the same way as a roll, meaning that no damage is taken during the dodge but that build-up from Status Effects is still inflicted.
 - Note that the direct damage from Blood Loss or Frostbite won't be taken if they fully applied during a dash, but the user will still be staggered out of the dash.
 - The damage from Madness and the stun from Madness and Sleep will still be inflicted, as will the Damage Negation decrease from Frostbite and the passive damage from Poison and Scarlet Rot.
- This skill is very similar to the skill Quickstep, however it covers a longer distance and grants more i-frames (16 or 14 vs 15 or 13) at the cost of more FP (5 vs 3).
- Very usable as a movement skill for movement-restricting areas such as as deep water or swamps.
 - Still very usable for this when out of FP, though the amount of i-frames will be heavily decreased so that should preferable only be used outside of combat for this.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Patch 1.06: Decreased the travel distance and invincibility frames of Ash of War: Bloodhound's Step while adding the changes below: Reduced performance when used continuously. Increased travel distance when on light equip load.
 - The "Reduced performance when used continously" means that the amount of i-frames granted on follow-up uses is decreased from 16 to 14 (effectively a 12.5% decrease in effectiveness for follow-up uses).

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Skill: Raptor of the Mists** is a Skill in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown: - Can be granted to any infusable melee weapon or thrusting shield with the Ash of War: Raptor of the Mists.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown:
Crouch down for a second, in readiness for an attack. If an attack would have hit during the crouch, the attack is dodged and the skill's user instead jumps up in a flash of feathers.

Any attack performed during the jump becomes a jumping attack.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- FP is only consumed if a hit was prevented by the crouch and thus triggers a jump. The crouch itself doesn't cost any FP.
- The crouch doesn't cost any points of Stamina, though it will stop any ongoing Stamina regeneration.
 - Any jumping light attack or jumping heavy attack used as a follow-up will consume the same amount of points of Stamina as they usually do.
- Since the user crouches down when the skill is activated, attacks that normally would have hit sometimes sail straight above their head and as such don't trigger the jump.
- The dodge from the crouch functions the same as a regular roll dodge, meaning that no damage is taken but the build-up from any Status Effects still takes effect.
 - As with a roll, the direct damage from Blood Loss and Frostbite is also avoided but the passive effects from Frostbite, Poison, and Scarlet Rot still take effect as do the effects of Sleep and Madness.
- As any attacks performed mid-air count as jumping attacks, their Attack Power is strengthened by the Claw Talisman and either Raptor's Black Feathers or Gravebird's Blackquill Armor.
- The user is briefly left vulnerable to attacks if they weren't hit during the crouch, as it takes a moment to stand up from the crouch during which the jump won't be triggered.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Patch 1.07: Reduced FP consumption.
 - FP cost when the dodge is activated was reduced from 14 to 6.
- Associated with the Ravenmount Assassins faction.
- Given that the Ravenmount Assassins idolize Deathbirds, the raptor referred to in the name of this skill is most likely also a Deathbird.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown:
Stomp and roar to send out a small air-based projectile with 110 base Strike Attack Power. Upon hitting a enemy or an object, a shockwave with 80 base Strike Attack Power that cannot hit the main target is created.

A 0 base Strike Attack Power is also created by the stomp.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 30 points of Stamina.
- Deals 6 Stance damage if the roar hits. Deals another 6 Stance damage at melee range, for 12 Stance damage in total.
- The Attack Power of the roar is boosted by 15% if the Roar Medallion is worn.
- The Attack Power of the roar is boosted by 10% if a Highland Axe is held in one of a character's active hand slots (this boost remains active even if the weapon with Beast's Roar is two-handed).
 - This boost does not stack with multiple Highland Axes.
- Range is slightly increased by the Arrow's Reach Talisman, though only be a very small amount.
- This is a bullet-type skill so its damage scales with the weapon's upgrade level and the user's Dexterity.
 - Dexterity-scaling is greatly increased if the weapon has a Keen Affinity, slightly increased if it has a Lightning Affinity, and somewhat increased on a Quality, Cold, Poison, or Blood Affinity, and greatly decreased if the weapon has a Heavy, Fire, Magic, or Occult Affinity.
 - Attack Power of the roar is always at least 440 (320 for adjacent targets) for a weapon at maximum upgrade level.
 - A Quality, Cold, Poison, or Blood and 45 Dexterity gives the roar 538 Attack Power (391 for adjacent targets), while a Lightning Affinity and either 45 or 80 Dexterity gives respectively 548 Attack Power (399 for adjacent targets) or 596 Attack Power (433 for adjacent targets), and a Keen affinity and either 45 or 80 Dexterity gives respectively 584 Attack Power (425 for adjacent targets) or 648 Attack Power (471 for adjacent targets).
- Very similar animation to the initial roar of skills such as War Cry and Barbaric Roar, lending it some potential for surprise against other players.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- This is the only Keen Affinity Skill that does not scale off of the weapon's attack rating, but instead from the Dexterity stat and weapon upgrade level.
- Runebears can also use this skill.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown:
Launches a short-ranged Magic projectile.

Can use a heavy attack to launch follow-up lunging thrust.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- As a Magic-based skill it benefits from the Spellblade's Set damage boost.
- Gains a 10% damage boost if used with a weapon that has the Magic affinity.
- The projectile part of the skill counts as a bullet-type and as such it scales with the weapon's upgrade level and the wielder's Intelligence.
 - Gains increased Intelligence-scaling depending on how strong the weapon's own Intelligence-scaling is, whether that be innate, or from the Magic or Cold affinities.
- The follow-up stab depends only on the weapon's own damage for its damage.
- The range of the projectile is quite short, often only barely outranging the follow-up thrust.
- The pebble deals minimal Stance damage, but the stab deals twice as much as a regular heavy attack, which ends up being roughly 20 Stance damage for most compatible weapons (exceptions are Daggers at a mere 12 Stance damage, and Thrusting Swords at 16 Stance damage).

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown: - Patch 1.06 increased the range of the projectile but decreased the damage and the stagger, preventing the projectile and the thrust from chaining into each other automatically.

sections.heading: Acquisition
